key_facts_for_researcher_to_verify.fact: Perpres No. 38 Tahun 2015 tentang KPBU dalam Penyediaan Infrastruktur is still the governing umbrella regulation; it revoked Perpres 67/2005 and its amendments (Perpres 56/2011, Perpres 66/2013).
key_facts_for_researcher_to_verify.confidence: high — confirmed in force via JDIH BPK; re-confirm no 2025/2026 replacement before publication

key_facts_for_researcher_to_verify.fact: Permen PPN/Kepala Bappenas No. 7 Tahun 2023 tentang Pelaksanaan KPBU dalam Penyediaan Infrastruktur is the CURRENT operational rulebook. It revoked Permen PPN No. 4 Tahun 2015 AND Permen PPN No. 2 Tahun 2020. It simplified the prastudi kelayakan from 8 kajian (under Permen PPN 2/2020) to 5 kajian, introduced provisions for KPBU skala kecil (Pasal 85), and tightened limits on financial-close extensions.
key_facts_for_researcher_to_verify.confidence: high — verify the exact kajian count and the Pasal 85 reference against the regulation text itself, not secondary blogs

key_facts_for_researcher_to_verify.fact: PT PII compiles the Buku Acuan Alokasi Risiko annually as a mandate under PMK No. 68 Tahun 2024 addressed to PT PII in its capacity as Badan Usaha Penjaminan Infrastruktur (BUPI). The 2025 edition groups project risks into 11 kategori risiko and is published openly on ptpii.co.id.
key_facts_for_researcher_to_verify.confidence: high — VERIFY the PMK 68/2024 number and the '11 kategori' count directly in the PDF before the writer states either

key_facts_for_researcher_to_verify.fact: RPJMN 2025-2029 infrastructure financing need estimated at ~USD 625 miliar (~Rp 10.350 triliun); some sources state >Rp 10.303 triliun. Projected composition: investasi pemerintah pusat & daerah 7,22%, investasi BUMN/D 6,13%, investasi swasta/masyarakat 86,65%.
key_facts_for_researcher_to_verify.confidence: medium — figure appears in secondary reporting; trace to a primary Bappenas/Kemenko document and pin the exact reference year before use

key_facts_for_researcher_to_verify.fact: Optimal risk allocation principle: risk is allocated to the party best able to manage or bear it. Private side generally absorbs construction, technology and operating-efficiency risk; government side generally retains policy/regulatory and certain force majeure risk. Land risk is a recognised distinct category.

Two investment-return schemes: Availability Payment (periodic government payment based on service availability meeting contracted quality — allocates revenue/demand risk to PJPK) and User Charge / user pay (return from end-user tariffs — allocates demand risk to the badan usaha).

Timing signals: KPBU project documents are typically prepared 3-4 years before operation; time to financial close has been publicly criticised as reaching about one year at the transaction stage; cooperation terms commonly run 10-15 years, and PJPK-side contract phases are described as spanning 20-30 years for some projects.
key_facts_for_researcher_to_verify.confidence: medium — these are practitioner/press characterisations, NOT a regulated standard. Must be framed as indicative ranges, never as a guaranteed timeline.

key_facts_for_researcher_to_verify.fact: Value for Money: KPBU carries preparation, transaction and contractual costs absent from conventional procurement. For small projects these ancillary costs can be high relative to project value, so VfM may come out negative and KPBU is then the wrong route.

Common causes of stalled KPBU projects: insufficiently credible project preparation, excessive political risk, marginal financial viability, and slow PJPK-side decision-making on project scope and financial commitments. Fasilitas Penyiapan Proyek / Project Development Facility (PDF) is the Kemenkeu facility that helps PJPK produce the final prastudi kelayakan and reach financial close.

KPBU skala kecil: Permen PPN 7/2023 sets no single cross-sector investment ceiling because thresholds differ per sector; a sector-specific illustration cited for air minum is an investment value around Rp 49 miliar with a maximum 10-year term and simple scope.
key_facts_for_researcher_to_verify.confidence: LOW — secondary practitioner blog only. Do NOT publish the Rp 49 miliar figure unless confirmed in a primary sector regulation. Safe fallback: state that no single cross-sector threshold exists.

gaps_to_exploit: REGULATORY FRESHNESS (biggest gap): virtually every ranking page anchors on Perpres 38/2015 alone and describes the process using the superseded Permen PPN 4/2015 or 2/2020 structure. Permen PPN/Bappenas 7/2023 — which revoked both, cut prastudi kelayakan from 8 kajian to 5, added KPBU skala kecil, and tightened financial-close extensions — has almost no clear, decision-useful explainer in the SERP. Only ahlikpbuindonesia.or.id (low authority) touches it.

DECISION THRESHOLDS: nobody in the top 10 answers 'should my project actually use KPBU?'. Kemenkeu's VfM pages are guideline-shaped, not decision-shaped. A genuine 'kapan KPBU BELUM tepat' section is unclaimed territory and is exactly the honest/counter-conventional trust-builder the style guide wants.

RISK ALLOCATION IN TABLE FORM: no ranking page presents a practitioner-usable 'who bears what' matrix. PT PII publishes the Buku Acuan Alokasi Risiko under a PMK mandate — a first-party authority asset no competitor can replicate.
STALE DATA ON THE HUB ITSELF: client hub still cites RPJMN 2020-2024. Supporting articles carrying RPJMN 2025-2029 figures refresh the cluster and give the hub current-cycle relevance.

FORMAT: the top 5 are portals and PDFs. Continuous, well-structured, extractable prose with tables and a real FAQ beats them on GEO/AI-Overview citation even where it cannot beat them on domain authority.
